topic.title: Efficient Language-Model Adaptation and Sparsity
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Adapting a pretrained language model can involve updating a small parameter subset, pruning computation, or transferring a learned adjustment across models. This topic studies those alternatives alongside model selection and limited-data scaling. Efficiency depends on which parameters and tokens remain active, and on whether adaptation preserves the capabilities needed downstream.
topic.whyItMatters: A method that saves trainable parameters may not reduce inference cost, while sparsity can alter both optimization and data reuse. Comparing approaches therefore requires explicit compute, memory, and data budgets. Reusable control mechanisms also need to handle differences in model vocabularies and behavior.
topic.evolution: A 2009 representative studies randomized pruning for dynamic programs, an earlier computational setting. Parameter-efficient transfer and movement pruning appear in later language-model work. Cross-model Control in 2024 learns a small portable logit adjustment; a 2026 scaling study analyzes how sparsity and repeated training interact when unique data are limited.
openQuestions: Which adaptation effects transfer across model families without degrading their original strengths?
How should sparsity be chosen jointly with data repetition and inference constraints?

papers.title: Bits That Count: Quantifying and Predicting Capabilities of Language Models

papers.title: BLISS: A Lightweight Bilevel Influence Scoring Method for Data Selection in Language Model Pretraining

papers.title: Certain Head, Uncertain Tail: Expert-Sample for Test-Time Scaling in Fine-Grained MoE

papers.title: Correctness-Optimized Residual Activation Lens (CORAL): Transferable and Calibration-Aware Inference-Time Steering
papers.tldr: CORAL uses regularized probes of internal activations to improve multiple-choice accuracy and confidence calibration during inference.

papers.title: Cram Less to Fit More: Training Data Pruning Improves Memorization of Facts

papers.title: Curriculum-Guided Layer Scaling for Language Model Pretraining

papers.title: Cutting LLM Evaluation Costs with SySRs: A Bandit Algorithm That Provably Exploits Model Similarity

papers.title: DAG-MoE: From Simple Mixture to Structural Aggregation in Mixture-of-Experts

papers.title: Data Difficulty and the Generalization–Extrapolation Tradeoff in LLM Fine-Tuning

papers.title: De-attribute to Forget for LLM Unlearning

papers.title: Decouple Searching from Training: Scaling Data Mixing via Model Merging for Large Language Model Pre-training

papers.title: Dirichlet-Prior Shaping: Guiding Expert Specialization in Upcycled MoEs

papers.title: From Parameters to Data: A Task-Parameter-Guided Fine-Tuning Pipeline for Efficient LLM Alignment

papers.title: Future-Gain Guided Test-Time Learning for Large Language Models

papers.title: HE-SNR: Uncovering Latent Logic via Entropy for Guiding Mid-Training on SWE-bench

papers.title: How to Train Your Advisor: Steering Black-Box LLMs with Advisor Models

papers.title: InfoLaw: Information Scaling Laws for Large Language Models with Quality-Weighted Mixture Data and Repetition

papers.title: Learning More from Less: Unlocking Internal Representations for Benchmark Compression

papers.title: Olmix: A Framework for Data Mixing Throughout LM Development

papers.title: OPIC: Enhancing Language Model Merging via Optimizing In-Context Capability

papers.title: Optimal Splitting of Language Models from Mixtures to Specialized Domains
